title: NaN Similarity, Zero Gradient | MLX & nntrainer Audit
description:
Can a vector fail to match itself? Two source-pinned numerical experiments reproduce implementation defects in MLX cosine similarity and nntrainer LayerNorm.

• MLX, FP16: cosine(x,x) with x=[1000,-1000,1000,-1000] returns NaN instead of 1. A separate zero-vector case has a NaN gradient despite a finite epsilon-regularized derivative.
• nntrainer LayerNorm, FP32 CPU: x=[-1,0,1,2], gamma=[1,2,4,8], dy=[1,1,1,1], beta=0, epsilon=1e-5, axis=3. The original input gradient is zero; its target is about [0.626,-0.537,-0.805,0.716]. Finite differences of the actual forward confirm it.

After local patches: 101 cosine tests pass on CPU and Metal; 42 nntrainer CPU tests pass. CPU baselines had 62 and 20 failures respectively. Key examples repeat in three fresh processes per audit.

https://github.com/nntrainer/nntrainer/blob/a7ea056e79ab8e14447ea305c1b634e233343258/nntrainer/layers/layer_normalization_layer.cpp

Scope: MLX Python source patch with official MLX/Metal 0.32.2; nntrainer native FP32 CPU on macOS arm64. No exact duplicate identified within recorded public searches. Maintainer confirmation, global novelty, version regression, performance and model-level impact are not established. No claim about particular Apple or Samsung devices. Known NVFP4 behavior and QuantizeLinear are excluded.

Narration uses a synthetic voice. Research and editorial review by Technology Product / GERO Research, with AI assistance. Original mathematical diagrams; no third-party footage, music, sponsorship or affiliate links.
